root_cause.text: The `qfq_change_class` function in `net/sched/sch_qfq.c` unconditionally frees the class structure and its associated qdisc during error cleanup, even when modifying an already existing class rather than a newly allocated one, leading to a use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff wraps the cleanup calls `qdisc_put(cl->qdisc)` and `kfree(cl)` under the `destroy_class` label inside an `if (!existing)` check, and the commit message states that "cl->qdisc and cl should only be freed if a new class and qdisc were allocated, or we risk various UAF."

net: sched: rename qdisc_destroy() to qdisc_put()

Current implementation of qdisc_destroy() decrements Qdisc reference
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 86bd446b5cebd783187ea3772ff258210de77d99
Author: Vlad Buslov <vladbu@mellanox.com>
Date:   Mon Sep 24 19:22:50 2018 +0300

    net: sched: rename qdisc_destroy() to qdisc_put()
    
    Current implementation of qdisc_destroy() decrements Qdisc reference
    counter and only actually destroy Qdisc if reference counter value reached
    zero. Rename qdisc_destroy() to qdisc_put() in order for it to better
    describe the way in which this function currently implemented and used.
bic_trace_step.reason: The `qfq_change_class` function contains the `destroy_class` error cleanup block (lines 528-531) which unconditionally calls `qdisc_put(cl->qdisc)` and `kfree(cl)` when an error occurs. This occurs even if the class `cl` was an already existing class being modified rather than a newly allocated one, leading to a use-after-free vulnerability.
